The test image shows a **pod** - one pod is split open revealing 2 light/cream-colored seeds inside. The pod is brown/tan, hairy (normal soybean texture), with some dark discoloration at the base tip. The other pod appears intact and elongated.

Pod-affecting classes to consider: Phomopsis, Purple_Seed_Stain, White_Mold, Anthracnose, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Green_stem_disorder.

The split/open pod with light cream seeds and brown pod coloring suggests Phomopsis. Let me check a reference.

The Phomopsis reference shows a clearly diseased pod with a shriveled, moldy, discolored seed. The test image seeds look round, plump, and cream-colored -- less severely diseased than the Phomopsis reference.

Re-evaluating the test image: open/split pod, 2 light cream round seeds, brown pod with dark discoloration at the base tip. This doesn't strongly match Phomopsis (shriveled seeds + gray mold), nor Purple_Seed_Stain (pink/purple seeds), nor White_Mold (fluffy white growth).

The pod's brown coloration, tip darkening, and premature-looking split could align with **Anthracnose** (dark lesions on pods, premature pod opening) or possibly **Phomopsis** at an early/mild stage. Given the dark discoloration at the pod base/tip and the split pod, Anthracnose remains a candidate (dark acervuli on pods). However the pod appearance without obvious black acervuli makes this uncertain.

The most consistent match overall with a split/open pod and the visible darkening pattern is Phomopsis (pod and stem blight) — early/mild infection before severe seed shriveling occurs.
